text:
Rasmus Dahlin is the minutes leader on a Buffalo team still trying to find its footing, playing 24.6 a night and logging more than 26 in several games this month. He has 15 points in 21 games, eight on the power play, and the Sabres have been a little better than even with him on at five on five: 52% of the shot attempts, 2.9 points of expected-goal share better than without him.

Nothing here screams luck in either direction. His goals match his chances and the team's finishing with him on is close to normal. The quieter stretch is real, though: six points in his last ten against eight expected, while Buffalo lost seven of those games. The Athletic's Matthew Fairburn called the win in Washington last week a night Dahlin and the team badly needed, and he had two points in it.

Evolving-Hockey had him 12th among defensemen in wins above replacement last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put his shot assists in the 99th percentile for his position. Our range has his scoring rate between 1.8 and 2.4 points per 60, above where he sits now. Watch the assists; they've lagged the work.
